rv.q: Stew is a play that will touch her spirit with laughter and will invoke family memories that will bring your eyes to tears.
In all, this excellent production, inspired by Zora Howard’s naturalistic comic drama is the result of close teamwork, just like the family portrayed in this play.
Howard here has done a remarkable job of portraying both the love and the pain these women share: two sides of the same coin, two bowls of the same stew.

What is completely brilliant about this show is the realness of the banter between the family, and how they use Shakespeare as a way to connect, show off to each other and how it foreshadows the ending.
Howard’s play rings of the things — the small things — that get forgotten in the befores and afters.
Malkia Stampley’s direction maintains a brisk pace that makes this Pulitzer Finalist script sing.
Shattered Globe Theatre’s production of “Stew”, written by Zora Howard and directed by Malkia Stampley, is nourishing, peppery, and full of spice.

cn.t: Critics praise this Pulitzer finalist as a gripping, emotionally powerful kitchen-sink drama about three generations of women. Strong performances, especially Austin's Mama, bring simmering family tensions to a boil in this satisfying production.
